items.title: Flu-like illness up 31% nationwide, with Central Visayas among the sharpest rises
items.summary: DOH counted 15,042 influenza-like illness cases nationwide from 1 to 14 October, up from 11,517 in the previous two weeks.
facts: Central Visayas is one of three regions with the highest percentage increases.
Dengue nationwide: 23,842 cases from 1 to 14 October, up 6% from the previous two weeks.
Leptospirosis nationwide: 554 cases from 1 to 14 October, down 54% from the previous two weeks.
items.alertNote: Regional figure. The report does not mention Bohol.

items.title: Child dies after suspected snakebite in Inabanga
items.summary: A 7-year-old girl reportedly died after a suspected cobra bite in Barangay Ubojan on the evening of 4 November.
facts: The bite reportedly happened shortly after 6 p.m. near her grandmother's house.
She was taken to Clarin Community Hospital and declared dead on arrival.
Details come from initial information. The report does not name an official source.

items.title: FDA warns against three skin-lightening creams flagged for mercury
items.summary: FDA advisories warn consumers not to buy or use Biogold Papaya Whitening Beauty Cream with Honey, Biocos Beauty Cream 3-in-1 Pack and Arayna Papaya Glow Beauty Cream.
facts: EcoWaste Coalition screening found mercury of about 13,310 to 16,930 ppm in the three products.
The products have no certificate of product notification, so selling them is illegal.
Children can be affected by mercury vapors and by sharing contaminated blankets, pillows and towels.
The advisories are national. The report names no Bohol sales or cases.

items.title: Free medical mission planned for Tagbilaran in February 2027
items.summary: The Tagbilaran Association of Northern California plans a mission with US-based doctors and expects about 1,500 patients.
facts: It will include dental care and free medicine, reading eyeglasses, and canes for seniors.
The venue is not final. Immaculate Heart of Mary Seminary in Taloto and Gallares Hospital are under consideration.

items.title: Code White for health facilities over Kalagkalag has ended
items.summary: DOH-7 put Central Visayas health facilities on Code White for All Saints' and All Souls' Day. The Bohol Provincial Health Office said it would deploy personnel to strategic areas.
facts: Government emergency rooms were told to stay ready for a possible patient surge.
DOH-7 advised avoiding unsafe water and questionable roadside food because of diarrhea risk.

items.title: DOH-7 put Central Visayas hospitals on heightened alert over haze
items.summary: Hospitals were told to prepare for a possible rise in respiratory illness. A draft circular was to be sent to the Bohol Provincial Health Office.
facts: As of 3 September, officials had recorded no haze-linked respiratory illnesses.
Children under five, older adults and pregnant women were told to limit outdoor activities.
items.alertNote: We found no later update, so check whether this still applies.

items.title: Philippine Red Cross Bohol steps up dengue response
items.summary: Volunteers are prioritizing Talibon, Tagbilaran City, Ubay, Getafe and Tubigon. Earlier drives ran in Balilihan and Candijay.
facts: Initial activities reached at least 307 people.
19 Red Cross Youth school councils committed to awareness campaigns and clean-ups.
The chapter activated its blood donor network for a 7-month-old dengue patient, who was later discharged.

items.title: Province-wide dengue outbreak declared in Bohol
items.summary: Governor Aumentado issued the declaration by executive order after cases exceeded the epidemic threshold for three consecutive weeks.
facts: 1,883 cases and 21 deaths from 4 January to 22 August 2026. This is the latest Bohol count we could confirm.
Talibon, Tagbilaran City, Ubay, Getafe and Tubigon were named as areas with a significant number of cases.
City and municipal health offices and hospitals were ordered to set up Dengue Fast Lanes.
Households, schools and communities were told to join Search and Destroy activities, including the 4 o'clock habit.
items.alertNote: Declared 27 August 2026. We found no report that it has ended.
items.highlightNote: named among the areas with a significant number of cases

items.title: Measles-rubella vaccination drive for Bohol and Cebu children has ended
items.summary: Ligtas Tigdas 2026 targeted at least 630,000 children aged 6 to 59 months across Cebu and Bohol.
facts: Rural health units took part, and barangay health workers helped register eligible children.
The report gives no Bohol-specific sites or schedules.

items.title: Report names the Bohol areas with the most new HIV cases
items.summary: Tagbilaran City, Panglao, Ubay, Tubigon and Talibon had the most new cases in Bohol from January to March 2025, the report says.
facts: Bohol recorded 17 new cases from January to March 2025.
Tagbilaran City and Panglao have the HIV treatment centers offering antiretroviral therapy.
A health worker quoted in the report said HIV is manageable with proper medication.

items.title: DOH Bohol urged masks, handwashing and flu shots
items.summary: DOH Bohol head Dr. Van Phillip Baton said flu and other respiratory infections remain among the province's top diseases to watch.
facts: Children, older adults, immunocompromised people and pregnant women are the groups named as vulnerable.
People at risk of complications should see a healthcare professional right away.

items.title: Leptospirosis cases rose sharply in Bohol after 2025 flooding
items.summary: Bohol logged 80 cases and five confirmed deaths from January to 22 November 2025, up 142.4% from the same period a year earlier.
facts: Provincial Health Officer Dr. Em-em Uy urged immediate consultation when symptoms appear.
Symptoms listed: fever, rashes, body pain, stomachache, vomiting and diarrhea.

items.title: Tagbilaran's PuroKalusugan brings free checkups to the purok
items.summary: The city's community health program offers free consultations and medicines, blood sugar tests, infant vaccination and PhilHealth enrollment.
facts: It started on 23 July 2025 at Purok 3, Barangay Dampas.
The report says it is expanding to other barangays but does not name them.
